controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where TESS saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · December 2022 and January 2023, mapped in this project
controls.notes: TOI-2267 in its own color, darker where its light in TESS's images of December 2022 and January 2023 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 17.5 hours its light rose and fell by 0.95%. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 1.2% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · TESS mission light curve, sector 20
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in TESS sector 20, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 0.95% as it turned once in 17.5 hours. The light curve is the mission's own; the criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) decide that it shows the star turning, and starry finds the map that reproduces it. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Step through the 8 maps to see the spots change.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from Gaia's spectrum of the star. The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere.
controls.notes: The color of the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum. 04 no model grid used here reaches it (Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 (ATLAS): 3030 is outside the grid 3500, 3750, 4000.; Reeve & Howarth (2016), MNRAS 456, 1294 (non-LTE TLUSTY): 3030 is outside the grid 27500, 30000, 32500, 35000, 37500, 40000, 42500, 45000, 47500, 50000, 52500, 55000.; Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 (PHOENIX): The grid must hold exactly one node at 3000 K, log g 5.). The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the TESS band at 3,030 K and log g 5.04 (u1 0.178, u2 0.514): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the TESS band at 3,030 K and log g 5.04 (u1 0.178, u2 0.514): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.
